a discrete walkie-talkie bleep-bloop when the handset starts up (and the same asset is the natural PTT/roger beep later). Source picked by the owner: the FIRST SECOND of ~/Downloads/walkie-talkie-radio-signal-activation-bosnow-1-00-02.mp3 — trim it, encode to the device's Opus/Ogg or raw PCM, ship it with the app, play it once the audio route is up. Respect the silent position (volume knob off = screen off), and note the route is only guaranteed after audio-mixer verifies it (bq268-alpine)

wata's SetupMixer runs ONCE at startup (go-pkgs/audio/audio_linux.go) and the codec resets its muxes when the Q6 comes up or restarts — `RX2 MIX1 INP1` to ZERO (silent speaker) and `DEC1 MUX` to ZERO (silent MICROPHONE: messages record, send and arrive as four seconds of nothing, which looks exactly like a kid who did not speak — cost a real send 2026-08-07). bq268-alpine's audio-mixer now applies-verifies-and-watches BOTH directions for two minutes after boot, so the boot race is covered; a mid-SESSION Q6 restart would still silence the app until reboot. Cheap fix: re-assert both muxes (or at least verify them) when a stream is opened — note mixer_open enumerates ~700 controls and is too slow mid-stream, so use a pre-opened handle like VolCtl. Oracles now exist: bq268-alpine `just mic-check` / `just speaker-check`
messages should sort most recent first in a conversation (and the conversation list by most recent activity) — today a kid scrolls to find what just arrived

exiting wata on the handset should offer a menu instead of just quitting: relaunch the app / reboot / poweroff / reboot to fastboot / reboot to EDL. Fastboot and EDL each need a second confirmation (they leave the device unusable to its user until someone with a cable intervenes). Note the device-side tools already exist in bq268-alpine (reboot-bootloader, reboot-edl)

design the arrival notification (plan doc first). A config toggle between: PLAY IMMEDIATELY, walkie-talkie style — except when the volume knob is off, which is also the screen-off/silent position — and a quiet mode that blinks the LED, shows an in-app banner and HIGHLIGHTS the conversation rather than only bumping a count, which a kid is unlikely to notice. Covers wata-fb (LED, speaker, screen state) and the mac client (its own quiet equivalent), (live arrival is verified working — see LIVE-UPDATE-MISSING)
